paper.title_en: BAQARO: Tracing Stochastic Black Hole Growth Histories and Quasar Lightcurves in a Cosmological Context
paper.abstract_en: How supermassive black holes (BHs) assemble their mass and power the luminous quasars we observe across cosmic time remain central open questions in galaxy evolution. We present BAQARO, a semi-empirical framework for BH growth. Built on subhalo merger trees extracted from the FLAMINGO-10k simulation, the model links BH growth histories to those of their host subhalos through prescriptions that capture both average trends and stochastic variability. BAQARO is constrained by the bolometric quasar luminosity function, the clustering of UV-luminous quasars, and the conditional Eddington ratio distribution function. With six free parameters controlling BH seeding, the coupling between gas accretion and halo growth, and the stochasticity and temporal coherence of accretion, the model reproduces the available observational constraints over $0 \lesssim z \lesssim 7$. Using emulators, we perform Bayesian inference and quantify the constraining power of each observable. Our main findings are: (i) BH accretion is well described by the assembly of cold gas reservoirs in halos, without requiring an explicit dependence on cosmic time. (ii) BHs rapidly assemble their mass at high redshift through stochastic episodes of super-Eddington accretion. (iii) These episodes are radiatively inefficient and persist for timescales of $\sim1\,\mathrm{Myr}$, imprinting observable signatures on quasar lightcurves, proximity zones, and clustering measurements. (iv) The merger growth channel is always subdominant, but becomes increasingly important at $z \lesssim 1$, particularly for massive BHs. BAQARO growth histories and quasar lightcurves provide a flexible framework for interpreting the rapidly expanding landscape of quasar observations, from high-$z$ accretion probed by JWST to low-$z$ mergers constrained by pulsar timing arrays.

decision.selection_reason_zh: 该论文提出了一个半经验框架BAQARO，将黑洞增长历史与类星体光变曲线联系起来，并以脉冲星计时阵列约束低红移合并。其与PTA的关联主要是通过合并通道的约束体现，具有潜在的相关性。
decision.title_zh: BAQARO：在宇宙学背景下追踪随机黑洞增长历史和类星体光变曲线
decision.abstract_zh: 超大质量黑洞（BH）如何积累其质量并驱动我们在宇宙时间中观测到的明亮类星体，仍然是星系演化中的核心开放问题。我们提出了BAQARO，一个用于黑洞增长的经验半框架。该模型建立在从FLAMINGO-10k模拟中提取的子晕合并树之上，通过捕捉平均趋势和随机变率的 prescriptions，将黑洞增长历史与其宿主子晕的增长历史联系起来。BAQARO受到热辐射类星体光度函数、紫外明亮类星体的成团性以及条件爱丁顿比分布函数的约束。该模型有六个自由参数控制黑洞播种、气体吸积与晕增长之间的耦合以及吸积的随机性和时间相干性，在 $0 \lesssim z \lesssim 7$ 范围内再现了可用的观测约束。使用 emulators，我们进行贝叶斯推断并量化每个观测量的约束能力。我们的主要发现是：(i) 黑洞吸积可以由晕中冷气体储库的组装很好地描述，而不需要明确依赖于宇宙时间。(ii) 黑洞通过超爱丁顿吸积的随机事件在高红移处快速积累其质量。(iii) 这些事件在辐射上是低效的，并持续约 $\sim1\,\mathrm{Myr}$ 的时间尺度，在类星体光变曲线、邻近区和成团性测量上留下可观测特征。(iv) 合并增长通道始终是次主导的，但在 $z \lesssim 1$ 时变得越来越重要，特别是对于大质量黑洞。BAQARO的增长历史和类星体光变曲线为解释迅速扩展的类星体观测领域提供了一个灵活的框架，从JWST探测的高红移吸积到脉冲星计时阵列约束的低红移合并。
